newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Dock strike halts 60 pct of Colombia coffee export.
newsitem.headline: Dock strike halts 60 pct of Colombia coffee export.

text.p: A strike by Colombian dock workers has paralyzed the 60 percent of the country's coffee exports that are shipped out through the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, private exporters said Wednesday.

The strike was called Tuesday night and began to bite Wednesday, leading to an order from the National Federation of Coffee Growers' to suspend all exports through the port until the strike was resolved, exporters said.
The dock workers halted all unloading and loading activities for an indefinite period to press for higher wage rises.
The government and employers' organizations set this year's rise in the minimum wage at 21.02 percent. That figure is then used as a benchmark for most wage rises in the private sector.
National Federation of Coffee Growers was not immediately available for comment on the effect of the dockers' strike.

Coffee exports were hard hit by a truck drivers' strike at the end of last year. Their demands for a rise in freight payments and other conditions have not been fully met but a spokesman for the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association said Wednesday there were no immediate plans to stage another strike.
